title: Data Quality and Best Practices
description: This SOP establishes data quality standards and best practices for SeaFoundry users. Consistent, high-quality data entry ensures reliable analytics, accurate reporting, and effective program management. Following these guidelines maintains data integrity across your organization.

steps.title: Understanding Data Completeness
steps.description: SeaFoundry tracks data completeness for each organism record using a Completeness Indicator (CompletenessIndicator). This appears in the Holdings Spreadsheet 'Complete' column showing a score and listing incomplete fields. A complete record has all recommended fields populated: Species, Provenance, Physical Form, Size, Health Status, and Life Stage. Strive for high completeness scores to enable accurate analytics and reporting. Incomplete fields limit filtering capabilities and may affect report accuracy.

steps.title: Required Data Fields
steps.description: Ensure these fields are always completed for new organism records:
checklistItems: Species: Select from the standardized species list. Never enter free-text species names.
Provenance/Genet: Link to an existing genet or create a new provenance record with proper source documentation.
Physical Form: Select the current physical form (Colony, Fragment, Micro-fragment, Recruit, etc.).
Size: Enter accurate size measurements using appropriate units and size band if applicable.
Health Status: Set initial health status. Update whenever health changes significantly.
Life Stage: Select appropriate life stage (Settler, Recruit, Juvenile, Adult, etc.).
Location: Ensure correct Site and Group (Structure) assignment.

steps.title: Photo Quality Guidelines
steps.description: When capturing evidence photos for observations, follow these guidelines:
checklistItems: Lighting: Ensure adequate lighting without harsh shadows. Natural daylight or dive lights work best.
Focus: Wait for camera to focus before capturing. Blurry images have limited diagnostic value.
Framing: Include the entire organism or affected area. Avoid cutting off edges of the subject.
Scale Reference: Include a scale reference (ruler, finger, standard object) when documenting size or extent.
Context: For disease/damage, capture both a close-up of affected tissue and a wider shot showing overall condition.
Consistency: For time-series documentation, photograph from the same angle each visit.
File Size: Standard resolution is sufficient. Very high resolution slows sync without adding value.

steps.title: Naming Convention Standards
steps.description: Consistent naming conventions enable efficient searching and organization:
checklistItems: Genet Local IDs: Use format SPECIES-NUMBER (e.g., ACER-001, OFAV-042). Species code should match standardized 4-letter codes.
Site Names: Use clear, location-based names. Include reef name or GPS reference area (e.g., 'Molasses Reef North', 'Key Largo Nursery').
Structure Names: Use descriptive names indicating type and position (e.g., 'Tree A-1', 'Table North-3', 'Coral Rope Line 5').
Observation Comments: Start with the key finding, then add details. Be specific but concise.
Avoid: Special characters, excessive abbreviations, all-caps, or personal names in identifiers.

steps.title: Using Standardized Dropdowns
steps.description: SeaFoundry uses standardized dropdown values configured in YAML files (e.g., mortality_causes.defaults.yaml, physical_form_constraints.yaml). Always select from dropdowns rather than entering free text when possible. This ensures data consistency and enables accurate filtering and reporting. If you need a value that doesn't exist, contact your organization administrator to request additions to the standardized lists rather than using workarounds.

steps.title: Health Status Consistency
steps.description: Apply health status ratings consistently using these definitions: 'Healthy' - normal coloration, no visible disease, active growth evident; 'Stressed' - visible stress signs but no disease, may show paling or reduced polyp extension; 'Diseased' - active disease lesions present; 'Recovering' - previously diseased/stressed now improving; 'Bleached' - significant loss of zooxanthellae, white or pale tissue; 'Damaged' - physical damage from predation, breakage, or abrasion. Document the reasoning in observation comments when changing status.

steps.title: Size Measurement Standards
steps.description: Record size measurements using the appropriate method for each physical form. The size specification (SizeSpec) supports multiple measurement types. For colonies, use maximum diameter. For fragments, use length or TLE (Total Linear Extension). Enter numeric values with appropriate units. Size bands provide categorical groupings when exact measurements aren't practical. Consistency is key: if your team uses TLE, all measurements should use TLE. Document your measurement protocol and train all team members.

steps.title: Error Correction Procedures
steps.description: When data errors are discovered, follow these correction procedures:
checklistItems: Wrong Organism Identified: Record an observation documenting the misidentification, then edit the organism record with correct species/genet information.
Incorrect Health Status: Update the health status and add an observation explaining the correction and actual condition.
Wrong Location Assignment: Use internal move to correct structure assignment. Add notes explaining the error.
Duplicate Records: Do not delete - mark one as archived with notes indicating it's a duplicate of the retained record.
Incorrect Mortality: Contact administrator - mortality events require special handling to reverse.
Data Entry Typos: Edit the field directly. Minor corrections don't require observation documentation.
Systematic Errors: For batch errors (e.g., wrong date on many records), contact administrator for bulk correction.

steps.title: CSV Import Validation
steps.description: When using CSV import for bulk data entry, validate your data before import. The UniversalCSVDialog includes a preview step showing how data will be imported. Check for: column mapping correctness, date format consistency, species code validity, and location path accuracy. The CSV Error Reporter (CSVErrorReporter) flags issues during import. Address all errors before confirming import. Keep original CSV files as backup documentation.

steps.title: Regular Data Audits
steps.description: Conduct periodic data quality audits using the Holdings Spreadsheet filters and Reporting tools. Check for: records with low completeness scores, organisms without recent observations, unusual health status patterns, orphaned records without valid genet links, and inconsistent naming patterns. Export data to CSV for offline analysis if needed. Document audit findings and corrections made. Schedule audits monthly or quarterly depending on data volume.

steps.title: Observation Comment Best Practices
steps.description: Write observation comments that are informative and searchable:
checklistItems: Be Specific: Instead of 'looks sick', write 'white lesion approximately 2cm on lower tissue edge'.
Include Context: Note relevant conditions - 'observed during heat wave, water temp 31C'.
Reference Previous: 'Lesion from 2024-01-10 observation has spread approximately 1cm'.
Use Standard Terms: Match terminology to dropdown options for searchability.
Avoid Assumptions: Document observations, not diagnoses unless confirmed.
Note Actions Taken: 'Applied antibiotic paste to lesion margin per disease protocol'.
Keep It Concise: Include essential information without excessive narrative.

steps.title: Data Integrity Safeguards
steps.description: SeaFoundry maintains audit trails for all changes. Original records are never permanently deleted - they are archived or marked with correction notes. Do not attempt to 'clean up' data by deleting historical records. If you notice data that appears incorrect, document it and discuss with your team before making changes. Batch operations are logged and can be reviewed. If you discover a significant data quality issue affecting multiple records, contact your administrator before attempting corrections to develop a proper remediation plan.

steps.title: Validation Rules
steps.description: SeaFoundry enforces validation rules defined in validation_rules.defaults.yaml. These include: required field enforcement, value range constraints, format validation, and cross-field consistency checks. When a validation error occurs, the form displays an error message indicating the issue. Address validation errors before saving. If you believe a validation rule is preventing legitimate data entry, document the scenario and request a rule review from your administrator.

steps.title: Team Training Recommendations
steps.description: Data quality is a team effort. Ensure all team members complete SeaFoundry training SOPs before entering data. Conduct periodic calibration sessions where team members compare how they would rate the same organisms to ensure consistency. Designate a data quality lead who reviews new entries and conducts audits. Create organization-specific guidelines building on these standards to address your unique species, sites, and workflows. Share lessons learned from data quality issues to prevent recurrence.
